trust_boundaries: TB-1: Internet/untrusted partners -> DMZ ingress edge (api_webhook, sftp_ingest)
TB-2: External data sources (kinesis_producer, pubsub_connector) -> ingestion tier (kafka_cluster, kafka_connect)
TB-3: Ingestion tier (kafka_cluster, kafka_connect) -> processing tier (flink_cluster, spark_batch, data_quality_checker)
TB-4: Processing tier -> storage raw zone (data_lake_raw)
TB-5: Raw zone -> curated zone / warehouse / feature store promotion boundary (data_lake_raw -> data_lake_curated -> data_warehouse, feature_store)
TB-6: Storage tier -> serving tier (feature_store, data_warehouse -> ml_model_registry, ml_serving_endpoint, bi_dashboard)
TB-7: Platform control plane (iam_service, airflow_orchestrator, data_catalog) -> all data-plane tiers
TB-8: AWS account <-> GCP project cross-cloud link (pubsub_connector -> kafka_cluster)
TB-9: Serving tier -> external consumers (ml_serving_endpoint API clients, bi_dashboard users)
architecture_summary.operational_context: Multi-cloud (AWS primary data plane + GCP source project) managed data platform: streaming and batch ingestion, medallion lake (raw/curated), warehouse, feature store and ML serving, orchestrated by Airflow with a central IAM control plane. Raw zone holds customer PII and partner financial records; curated zone and feature store hold de-identified but re-identifiable data. Serving tier exposes an inference API and BI dashboards to internal users and authenticated external API clients.

threat_actors.name: Opportunistic external attacker / commodity botnet operator
threat_actors.motivation: Low-effort monetisation: credential stuffing against the webhook and SFTP edges, scanning for exposed storage, cryptomining or data resale
threat_actors.initial_access_vector: Internet-exposed api_webhook and partner sftp_ingest; leaked access keys found in public repositories
non_capabilities: No zero-day development budget; relies on public exploits and default/leaked credentials
No physical access to datacentres or insider knowledge of internal schema and role names
Cannot defeat enforced MFA or workload-identity federation on the IAM control plane
No ability to sign or forge model artifacts accepted by the registry
No persistence capability against immutable, object-locked storage buckets

threat_actors.name: Motivated data broker / organised fraud group
threat_actors.motivation: Bulk exfiltration and resale of customer PII and partner financial records; model evasion to enable downstream fraud
threat_actors.initial_access_vector: Phishing a data engineer for cross-cloud static keys, then using the platform's own processing tier to reach the lake and feature store
non_capabilities: No nation-state-grade network implant on the cloud interconnect; TLS interception requires a compromised proxy
Cannot obtain insider approval to merge a DAG or connector plugin into the production repository
Limited budget for model-extraction campaigns against a rate-limited inference API
No ability to disable cross-region backup replication or object lock retention
Cannot compel a third-party SaaS provider (BI vendor, connector marketplace) to act on their behalf

threat_actors.name: Malicious or negligent insider (data engineer / analyst with production access)
threat_actors.motivation: Financial gain from data sale, sabotage after notice, or reckless handling of production data for convenience
threat_actors.initial_access_vector: Legitimate DAG authoring rights in airflow_orchestrator, warehouse query access, or BI export permissions
non_capabilities: Cannot bypass break-glass approval for deleting object-locked curated prefixes
No access to the cloud root accounts or to KMS key policy administration
Cannot alter immutable raw-zone objects once written (write-once retention)
Actions in the control plane are logged to an append-only audit trail they cannot edit
No ability to modify model artifacts without a second reviewer approving the registry promotion

attack_paths.entry_point: Public HTTPS webhook endpoint on the internet edge (TB-1)
attack_paths.impact: Foothold inside the ingestion edge; forged events injected into kafka_cluster and propagated through processing into curated data and models
attack_paths.likelihood_rationale: The endpoint is internet-reachable, parses attacker-controlled payloads with custom code, and no WAF/rate limit is confirmed in front of it.

attack_paths.entry_point: Partner SFTP endpoint reachable from the internet with shared accounts (TB-1)
attack_paths.impact: Attacker-supplied files are treated as trusted partner data by kafka_connect and enter the lake; persistent ingestion-tier foothold
attack_paths.likelihood_rationale: Partner onboarding uses long-lived shared SFTP credentials and IP allowlisting is only partially enforced.

attack_paths.entry_point: Long-lived cloud access keys leaked from CI/CD or a developer workstation, replayed against IAM/STS (TB-7)
attack_paths.impact: Cross-account access to data_lake_raw, data_lake_curated, data_warehouse and Kafka control plane; full data-plane compromise from a single credential
attack_paths.likelihood_rationale: Static cross-cloud automation keys exist with no enforced rotation and no MFA requirement for programmatic sessions.

attack_paths.technique_name: Compromise Software Supply Chain: Compromise Software Supply Chain
attack_paths.entry_point: Third-party Kafka Connect connector plugin pulled from a public marketplace into the ingestion runtime (TB-2)
attack_paths.impact: Code execution inside the ingestion VPC under the connector service account, with persistence across task restarts
attack_paths.likelihood_rationale: Connector plugins are version-pinned but not signature-verified, and marketplace artifacts are pulled from an untrusted tier.

attack_paths.entry_point: DAG authoring rights or a hijacked Airflow UI session in platform services (TB-7)
attack_paths.impact: Arbitrary Python execution on workers holding data-plane credentials; ability to tamper with every downstream processing job
attack_paths.likelihood_rationale: Airflow is a credentialed control plane and the DAG repository is broadly writable by the data engineering group, with review only informally enforced.

attack_paths.entry_point: Compromised ingestion container reaching Flink TaskManagers over a flat east-west network (TB-3)
attack_paths.impact: Lateral movement from the ingestion tier into the processing tier; streaming state and job credentials exposed
attack_paths.likelihood_rationale: Ingestion and processing share VPC peering with broad east-west rules and no mTLS between tiers.

attack_paths.entry_point: Over-permissive bucket policy exploited with a compute role obtained via AP-003 or AP-005 (TB-4)
attack_paths.impact: Bulk exfiltration of raw PII and partner financial records at rest
attack_paths.likelihood_rationale: The raw zone is readable by broad analyst and pipeline roles and there is no data-perimeter restriction to trusted VPCs.

attack_paths.entry_point: Write access to curated-zone Spark jobs or to data_quality_checker promotion thresholds (TB-5)
attack_paths.impact: Silent corruption of curated datasets feeding the warehouse, feature store and models; fraudulent downstream business decisions
attack_paths.likelihood_rationale: Curated writes are performed by multiple overlapping jobs and quality thresholds are editable by job owners, with only partial integrity checks.

attack_paths.entry_point: Compromised role with delete permissions on curated-zone prefixes (TB-5)
attack_paths.impact: Loss of curated datasets, blocking warehouse refresh, feature generation and model retraining
attack_paths.likelihood_rationale: Object lock/versioning and cross-region replication are implemented, materially limiting destructive blast radius.

attack_paths.entry_point: Cross-cloud GCP Pub/Sub to AWS Kafka transport traversing a shared interconnect/egress proxy (TB-8)
attack_paths.impact: Interception or modification of data in transit, plus capture of SASL/API credentials used by the bridge
attack_paths.likelihood_rationale: Most hops use TLS, but one connector still negotiates SASL_PLAINTEXT and a legacy proxy terminates TLS without pinning.

attack_paths.entry_point: Compromised BI analyst account or dashboard service principal exporting warehouse marts (TB-9)
attack_paths.impact: Exfiltration of aggregated customer and commercial data to attacker-controlled cloud storage outside the trust boundary
attack_paths.likelihood_rationale: BI export to cloud storage is permitted by design and warehouse-level egress filtering or DLP on exports is not enforced.

attack_paths.entry_point: Unsigned model artifact or poisoned dependency promoted from a public hub or compromised data-science workstation (TB-6)
attack_paths.impact: Backdoored model served by ml_serving_endpoint producing attacker-chosen outputs for trigger inputs, while behaving normally otherwise
attack_paths.likelihood_rationale: Model artifacts are versioned but not cryptographically signed, and dependencies are pulled from untrusted public hubs without provenance attestation.

attack_paths.entry_point: Weakly authenticated scoring API reachable by external clients with high-volume queries (TB-9)
attack_paths.impact: Model inversion and membership inference recovering sensitive feature_store attributes present in training data
attack_paths.likelihood_rationale: Query quotas exist but responses return confidence scores that aid inversion and there is no per-client anomaly detection.

attack_paths.entry_point: Adversarially crafted records injected via api_webhook/kafka and carried through feature_store into inference (TB-6)
attack_paths.impact: Fraud and abuse detection bypassed at inference time; crafted features persist in the feature store affecting future scoring
attack_paths.likelihood_rationale: Only statistical drift checks exist in data_quality_checker; no adversarial-input detection or per-record anomaly gating is applied before scoring.

mitigations.control_name: Boundary protection for the public webhook: WAF, strict JSON/schema validation, request signing and per-source rate limiting
Remote access management for partner file transfer: per-partner keys, source-IP allowlisting, MFA-backed portal and session logging
Identity and credential lifecycle: eliminate static keys in favour of short-lived workload identity, enforce rotation and MFA for privileged roles
Leverage vetted modules and services: connector allowlist, signed images (cosign) and admission control rejecting unverified plugins
Controlled maintenance of orchestration assets: Airflow RBAC, protected DAG branch with mandatory review, sandboxed and least-privilege workers
Network integrity and segmentation: deny-by-default security groups between ingestion and processing, mTLS between tiers, no flat east-west path
Data-at-rest protection for the raw zone: deny-by-default bucket policies, SSE-KMS with per-zone keys, VPC-endpoint-only access and sensitive-data discovery scanning
Integrity checking for curated data: table-format snapshots, row-count and checksum reconciliation, immutable raw zone and change review on quality thresholds
Backups with immutability: object lock retention on curated prefixes, cross-region replication and tested restore runbooks
Data-in-transit protection: TLS 1.2+ and mTLS on all Kafka and cross-cloud hops, private interconnect, removal of SASL_PLAINTEXT and certificate pinning on the bridge
Protection against data leaks: warehouse/BI egress filtering, DLP on bulk exports, approved-destination allowlist and export volume alerting
ML artifact integrity: model signing and SBOM verification, trusted-registry-only pulls and dual-approval promotion into ml_model_registry
Inference API abuse control: authenticated per-client quotas, output minimisation (coarse confidence bands) and query-pattern anomaly detection
Continuous monitoring for model inputs: feature-distribution drift detection, adversarial-input screening in data_quality_checker and per-record anomaly gating before scoring

findings.severity_rationale: Internet-reachable parsing endpoint with attacker-controlled payloads gives a straightforward path into the ingestion tier, though only partial confidentiality and availability impact is expected initially.
Shared long-lived partner SFTP credentials grant authenticated write access to a pipeline that treats uploaded files as trusted, yielding high integrity impact on downstream data.
A single leaked static key yields cross-account access spanning raw, curated, warehouse and Kafka control plane, so one credential compromises the entire data platform.

Unsigned third-party connector code executes inside the ingestion VPC under a service account with broker and storage reachability, and the high attack complexity is offset by full post-exploitation impact.

Airflow workers hold broad data-plane credentials, so a single privileged DAG-author account yields code execution and control over all processing jobs; privileged-only access keeps it below Critical.
Flat east-west networking permits pivot from ingestion into processing, but the pivot requires an existing foothold and yields limited confidentiality and integrity impact within one VPC.
The raw zone holds restricted PII readable by broad pipeline and analyst roles over any network path, making bulk collection of data at rest a high-impact, low-complexity objective.
Tampering at the curated promotion boundary silently corrupts warehouse, feature store and model inputs, producing high integrity and confidentiality impact that is difficult to detect and reverse.
Destructive action on curated prefixes would disrupt analytics and retraining, but implemented object lock, versioning and cross-region replication reduce availability impact to a recoverable outage.
A partially unencrypted cross-cloud hop exposes data in transit, but the low likelihood of positioned interception and the confidentiality-only impact keep the rating at medium.

The BI export path deliberately permits bulk movement of warehouse data to external cloud storage, so a compromised analyst or service principal can exfiltrate aggregated commercial data with low effort.

An unsigned backdoored model served to production clients gives an attacker durable, scoped control over automated decisions while metrics remain normal, with cross-boundary impact into serving consumers.
Inference API extraction requires sustained high-volume querying and yields only aggregate leakage of training features, so partial rate limiting and output granularity keep the rating at medium.
Crafted inputs can evade the served model and persist in the feature store, but the effect is bounded to decision quality on a single model family and requires specificity about model behaviour.

tool_call_scope: ml_model_registry artifact pull at deploy time
airflow_orchestrator triggered retraining job submission (human-approved DAG run)
agentic.blast_radius: No autonomous tool-calling agent exists; automation is limited to scheduled Airflow jobs and model inference. An uncontrolled run could affect: curated and feature-store data integrity for downstream models, decisions emitted by ml_serving_endpoint to external API clients, and compute cost across the processing tier. It cannot directly mutate IAM policy, delete object-locked raw data, or invoke external third-party APIs.
human_oversight_points: Data engineer review and merge approval for every Airflow DAG and connector configuration change
Dual approval required to promote a model artifact into ml_model_registry and to the serving endpoint
Analyst-confirmed review of BI exports above threshold volume
Break-glass approval workflow for any deletion or retention change on curated-zone prefixes
